newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares drop again in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares drop again in quiet trade.

text.p: Jordanian shares fell slightly at end of weekly trade on Wednesday with some portfolio buying to bolster the end-of-year balance sheet in the quietest trading day of the month.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index dropped 0.09 percent to 151.16 points in business worth just 355,644 ($502,322).

It was the lowest trading volume since sanction-hit Iraq announced last month it had reached agreement with the United Nations to resume limited oil exports, raising business hopes in neighbouring Jordan.
Unified Transport Company, a trucking firm expected to benefit from the oil-for food deal, rose 0.06 dinars to close at 2.06 dinars, in the busiest trade of the day with a 90,884 dinars turnover.
National Industries, one of the firms that have clinched new export deals, fell back 0.02 dinars to 0.71 in one of the heaviest business of the day, in deals worth a total 59,000 dinars.
Mideast Hotels and Jordan Selpho Chemicals were the top gainers with a 5.10 percent and 5 percent rise respectively in moderate trade.
Insurance company Al-Nisr al-Arabi continued its unpward trend to rise 4.8 percent to 5.60 dinars on expectations that the one million dinar capitalised firm could issue a 20 percent cash dividend.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange rose 0.08 percent to 82.38 points from 82.32 points, still 13.74 percent down from the start of the year.
Rising shares outnumbered losers on Wednesday by 17 to 13, with shares in ten other firms trading but closing unchanged.
